title: mlsys-2026-notes-energy-aware-inference
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad from MLSys 2026 (talks + poster session) focused on energy-aware inference techniques and system-level tricks we might pilot at Redwood. Rough, half-formed ideas + concrete experiment plans. Not polished.

Topline takeaways:
- Energy matters: several papers show 20–40% runtime energy reductions for transformer inference with modest quality loss using mixed strategies (quantization + early exit). Worth exploring because Dedicated and Private customers care about TCO and carbon budgets.
- KV cache tiling matters more than we thought: papers comparing cache shard placement across GPUs show big latency tail wins when aligning cache partitions with persistent model shards (especially for long-context streaming).
- Sparse MoE routing at inference time can reduce compute for a subset of requests, but requires coordination with batching and routing layer to avoid variance in latency.

Interesting papers / talks to follow up (my shorthand):
- "GreenStream: energy-aware streaming inference" (poster) — idea: adapt token compute per prefix using lightweight predictor that estimates next-token perplexity. Low-cost predictor runs on CPU, triggers quantized path.
  - Key hack: maintain tiny LRU of recent predictions to avoid re-evaluating predictor for very common prefixes.
  - Implementation note: could be integrated as a pre-routing hook in Redwood's smart routing.

- "KVStripe: cache tiling across GPUs for long context" — evaluation shows 30% latency p99 reduction for streaming with 128k cache by colocating hot prefixes.
  - Link: arXiv 2601.01234 (linked above).
  - Thought: apply to Dedicated pools where we can control placement; for Hosted API perhaps best-effort via routing policy: route requests with active sessions to same node-set.

- "Lite-MoE: inference-friendly gating" — routing simplified to deterministic hash on prefix clusters, reduces routing jitter, but needs model-level compatibility.
  - Idea: rather than full MoE, we might emulate via conditional quantization profiles per-request, cheaper to roll out.

Engineering implications for Redwood (brain-dump):
- Routing layer capabilities to add:
  1) session affinity / hot-prefix hints (sticky routing but cross-region-aware), controlled by per-customer policy.
  2) pre-routing classifier hook (CPU) that returns a small set of candidate model/quant profiles; used to decide whether to send to "low-power" variant.
  3) cache-aware placement API on Dedicated: allow customers to opt into colocating session-state heavy workloads.

Experiment backlog (concrete, prioritized):
- EXP-1 (fast): baseline measuring p50/p95/p99 and joules/token for a 13B model under three runtime modes: float32 baseline, int8 quantized, hybrid (early-exit top-k heuristic). Run on single Dedicated node with 4xA100-equivalent. Metrics: latency, token energy (via nvidia-smi power sampling), quality (perplexity & small prompt eval). Owner: me. Timebox: 2 weeks. Linked JIRA: RWD-2345.
- EXP-2 (mid): implement sticky-session routing prototype in staging that pins sessions to a GPU subset for 24h; measure cache hit rates and tail latency for streaming chat workloads. If hit-rate improves >15% then expand test. Owner: Samir. Timebox: 3 weeks.
- EXP-3 (risky): integrate tiny CPU predictor (GreenStream idea) as a pre-hook; test on low-traffic canary. Measure mispredictions cost vs saved energy. Owner: Iris. Timebox: 6 weeks.

Quick sketches / pseudo-architecture notes (for the above):
- Pre-hook classifier API shape: (session_id, prefix_hash, recent_tokens_meta) -> {profile_id: str, confidence: float, sticky_hint: bool}
- Router decision flow: if confidence > 0.8 AND profile_id == "low_power" then route to low_power_pool ELSE route normally.
- Cache tiling plan: maintain per-shard "prefix hotness" = LRU counters exported to controller; controller tries to allocate hot shards to same node; if churn high, fall back to routing policy that biases towards affinity.

Open questions (capture now so I don't forget):
- How noisy are power measurements at per-request granularity? nvidia-smi sampling is coarse — need to instrument host-level power rails or integrate with cloud provider power metrics.
- What's customer appetite for slightly lower quality / faster / cheaper response? Need to sync with solutions-eng for candidate pilot customers.
- Billing model: how to reflect energy-optimized variants? discount? separate SKU?

Random notes & references from sessions / people I spoke to:
- Talk: "Prefetching KV-cache entries for interactive apps" — prefetcher must be conservative; false prefetches cost more than misses for small prompt lengths.
- Slack fragment: #infra-ops thread about RWD-402 capacity planning for Dedicated pools — @maria linked a capacity table that could be used for EXP-2.
- GitHub: runtime PR that touches batching heuristics might conflict with pre-hook patch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/812 (watch out).

Action items (next 7 days):
- Share EXP-1 plan with Samir + Iris, create short RFC doc in drive (I will draft).
- Reach out to Solutions Eng (cc: Maya Chen) to find 1 customer pilot candidate interested in cost-optimized inference.
- Add a tiny note in product backlog: "billing model for energy-optimized routes".

Unresolved TODOs (for later):
- Flesh out metrics instrumentation for joules/token across cloud providers.
- Prototype tiny predictor (GreenStream) on CPU and run microbenchmarks to estimate overhead.

Notes-to-self (loose thoughts):
- Could we offer an "eco-mode" in the Redwood Console where customers toggle and see projected $/month savings? Nice GTM asset.
- For Private deployments, air-gapped inference boxes could use local power sensors for more accurate accounting — ask Security & Deployables if that's acceptable for audits.

End of scratchpad. Will convert key parts into RFC + backlog items if experiments show promise.
